newsitem.title: USA: More layoffs at Station's Missouri casino.
newsitem.headline: More layoffs at Station's Missouri casino.

text.p: Despite drawing large crowds, Station Casinos Inc has laid off another 325 workers at its two month-old Missouri casino, a company spokesman said Friday.
Since it opened Jan 16 with 3,400 employees, the $300 million gambling and entertainment complex has eliminated 974 positions, or about 29 percent of the original workforce.

Joe Keenan, a spokesman for the casino, told Reuters the company does not currently expect to reduce its workforce any further, but he cautioned that Station was always looking for ways to maximize profits.
Jay Sevigny, Station's Midwest operations president, was quoted in Friday's Kansas City Star newspaper as saying that the layoffs were the result of overstaffing.
The most recent workforce reduction came amid news that large crowds flocked to Station's Kansas City casino in February.

Data released Thursday by the Missouri Gaming Commission showed that 838,590 people passed through Station's turnstiles in February. That figure represented 43.7 percent of the combined February admissions at all five casinos in the Kansas City area.
Also in February, Station Kansas City reported $11.74 million in adjusted gross revenue, which reflects casinos' pre-tax operating income from all wagers and after winners have been paid.
That figure represented 50.6 percent of the combined adjusted gross revenue for the entire Kansas City casino market during the same month.
